title: Cross-account aggregate quota views and external billing hooks PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Large customers run multiple Redwood accounts (per-team or per-environment) and ask for a consolidated view of quota consumption, predictable overage handling across accounts, and a way to export billing events into their ERP systems. Current per-account quotas and invoice line item model forces manual reconciliation and creates surprise overages.

Goal: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for two related capabilities: (1) aggregate quota views and cross-account soft-pooling (dashboard and API) and (2) external billing hooks that emit line-level metering events for customers to ingest into external billing/ERP systems. Aim for minimal latency in reporting (under 5 minutes for line events), clear proration rules, and explicit entitlements mapping so Dedicated/Private customers retain isolation guarantees while enabling cross-account billing visibility for authorized org admins.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregate dashboard shows cumulative monthly consumption (tokens, embeddings, concurrency) for a configurable set of accounts with per-account drilldown and comparison view.
API endpoint /v1/aggregates returns consistent aggregated usage for requested window (start/end) within 60s of query for historical windows and within 5 minutes for near-real-time windows.

Soft-pool policy: Admin can enable 'soft pooling' between N accounts belonging to an organization; soft pooling provides pre-defined burst credits that draw across accounts but preserves per-account quotas for billing clarity. Enabling requires explicit admin consent and audit log entry.

Overage handling: When soft pool is exhausted, system generates per-account overage events following configured priority (account-first or org-first) and creates invoice draft items with clear origin account mapping.

External billing hooks: Customers can register HTTPS endpoints and a signing key. For each billable event (metering window or overage), Redwood sends an HTTP POST containing a single-line CSV payload and a signature header. Retries follow exponential backoff up to 6 attempts; eventual failures are logged and surfaced to admins.
Invoice transparency: Invoices include origin account id for each line item and a human-readable reason code (e.g., TOKEN_OVERAGE, BURST_CREDIT, RESERVED_CAPACITY_FEE).
RBAC: Only org admins with explicit 'billing:aggregate' permission can configure pools, register hooks, or view aggregated dashboards. All actions recorded in audit logs (user, timestamp, IP).

Backfill correctness: When a historical backfill is requested (e.g., import usage from on-prem agent), aggregated results must match exported per-account usage within 0.1% token variance for windows >24h.
Performance: Dashboard queries for orgs with up to 500 accounts complete within 3s for cached windows; API queries complete within 10s under normal load.
Documentation: PRD linked runbook and public docs created for enterprise customers including example webhook consumer, security guidance, and troubleshooting steps.
scope_changes: Initial scope included a full billing reconciliation engine; scope reduced to external billing hooks (export only) and invoice draft line items to avoid rebuilding invoicing provider during first iteration.
Decision to postpone cross-region aggregation (APAC/EU) to next cycle due to data residency review.
Added requirement for explicit admin consent and audit trail after legal review highlighted consent and auditability as must-haves for enterprise procurement.
tradeoffs: Push vs Pull model for external hooks: Chose push (webhooks) for near-real-time events even though it increases retry complexity; pull (s3/export) deferred as a lower-latency-batch alternative in roadmap.
Soft pooling semantics: Opted for configurable priority (account-first vs org-first) to balance predictability vs cost-centralization, accepting added UI complexity.
Invoice integration: Emit draft line items only (no automatic charging) to avoid coupling with multiple external billing systems in MVP.
